data.narrative:
Valinor Enterprises, a Series A–stage Defense & Security company founded by Trae Stephens and Grant Verstandig, is evaluated against a peer universe of 11 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies (2 public, 8 private). The peer set includes both Series B comparables such as Dream Security ($3.0B), Allen Control Systems ($2.2B), and Harmattan AI ($1.4B), as well as earlier-stage private firms including Anduril Industries and Helsing.

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.0x multiplier to Valinor's $85M+ total raised, yielding an implied value of $170M based on typical Series A step-up dynamics. Peer-median analysis across the 11-company comparables universe produces $1.0B, reflecting a range from $125M to $3.0B. The dispersion reflects heterogeneity in capital efficiency and market positioning within the defense-tech sector.

Triangulation of both methods yields a median valuation of $585M, with a low-end estimate of $144M and high-end estimate of $1.1B. The wide range—spanning roughly 8x from low to high—reflects the early-stage profile of the target relative to later-stage Series B peers in the comparison set. Key uncertainties include customer traction, deployment maturity, and relative competitive positioning within a market where valuations span an order of magnitude.
